topics.title: Ohm’s law in a material
topics.idea: Current density responds to the local electric driving field.
topics.result: $\mathbf J=\sigma\mathbf E$ for an ohmic conductor at rest; $R=\ell/(\sigma A)$.
topics.explain: For a straight uniform wire, $J=I/A$ and $E=V/\ell$.::Uniform cross-section and steady flow allow constant averages.;;Substitute into $J=\sigma E$ and rearrange.::The same local response applies throughout the wire.;;Power converted to heat per volume is $\mathbf J\cdot\mathbf E$.::Field work per charge times charge flow gives energy transfer.
topics.trap: Conductivity $\sigma$ is not a surface charge density in this topic; its unit is S/m.
topics.check: If length doubles at fixed area and conductivity, what happens to R?=>R doubles.

topics.title: Electromotive force
topics.idea: An emf accounts for energy supplied around a circuit per unit charge.
topics.result: $\mathcal E=\oint\mathbf f\cdot d\mathbf l$ where f is driving force per unit charge.
topics.explain: A battery's chemical source pushes charge against an electrostatic potential rise.::Electrostatic forces alone have zero closed-loop work.;;In a moving circuit the magnetic part $\mathbf u\times\mathbf B$ can contribute to the circuit emf.::u is the velocity of the conductor element.;;An emf need not equal the terminal voltage of a source delivering current through internal resistance.::Some source energy is dissipated internally.
topics.trap: The symbol emf denotes volts, not newtons.
topics.check: A battery has emf 12 V, internal resistance 1 Ω and supplies 2 A. Terminal voltage?=>10 V.

topics.title: Motional emf and energy supply
topics.idea: A moving conductor cuts magnetic flux and separates charge.
topics.result: $\mathcal E= B\ell v$ for mutually perpendicular B, rod length and velocity.
topics.explain: Charges moving with the rod feel $q\mathbf v\times\mathbf B$.::Lorentz force separates signs along the rod.;;The emf along it has magnitude $Bv\ell$.::Integrate the force per charge along its length.;;A closed resistive circuit carries $I=B\ell v/R$ and has magnetic drag $F=B I\ell$.::The induced current opposes the increasing flux.;;Mechanical power $Fv$ equals $I^2R$ in steady motion.::The pulling agent supplies the electrical energy.
topics.trap: The magnetic field itself does no work on individual charges; the external mechanical agent supplies the heat.
topics.check: Double v in the same circuit. How does heating change?=>I doubles, so $I^2R$ quadruples.

topics.title: Faraday’s law and Lenz’s rule
topics.idea: Changing magnetic flux creates an emf that opposes the flux change.
topics.result: $\mathcal E=-d\Phi_B/dt$ for a loop; $\mathcal E=-N\,d\Phi_B/dt$ for N identical turns.
topics.explain: Choose the positive area normal and path orientation first.::The flux and emf signs must be linked.;;Calculate changes in B, area or angle, not only B.::Any of these changes can alter flux.;;Apply the minus sign and infer the current direction.::The induced field opposes the change, not necessarily the original field.
topics.trap: Flux can be zero at an instant while its derivative and emf are nonzero.
topics.check: A positive flux is increasing. Is the emf positive or negative in the matching orientation?=>Negative.

topics.title: Induced electric field
topics.idea: A changing B creates circulating E even where no conducting wire is present.
topics.result: $\oint\mathbf E\cdot d\mathbf l=-d\Phi_B/dt$; $\nabla\times\mathbf E=-\partial\mathbf B/\partial t$.
topics.explain: For an axially symmetric changing B, choose a circular path.::Symmetry makes E tangential and equal along the circle.;;Inside a uniform-field disk, enclosed flux is $B\pi r^2$.::Only the area inside the path contributes.;;Outside a disk of radius a, enclosed flux is $B\pi a^2$.::B is confined to the disk, so added area contributes no flux.;;Divide the flux derivative by $2\pi r$ to find signed $E_\phi$.::The line integral is E times the circumference.
topics.trap: An induced E generally cannot be written as only $-\nabla V$ with a single-valued scalar V.
topics.check: Can a test charge experience induced E outside the region containing B?=>Yes. The enclosed changing flux gives nonzero circulation.

topics.title: Self and mutual inductance
topics.idea: Inductance measures how strongly circuit current links magnetic flux.
topics.explain: In a fixed linear geometry, magnetic field is proportional to current.::Superposition applies.;;Flux linkage therefore scales with current.::The coil area and turns are fixed.;;Differentiate the linkage and use Faraday's law.::A changing current induces an opposing emf.;;Mutual inductance links two circuits; reciprocity gives $M_{12}=M_{21}$ for ordinary reciprocal linear media.::The mutual magnetic energy is symmetric.
topics.trap: L is a circuit property with units henry, not a resistance. The negative sign belongs to induced emf; passive voltage drop uses $+L\,dI/dt$.
topics.check: What current change induces 1 V in 0.20 H?=>A rate magnitude of 5 A/s.

topics.title: Magnetic field energy
topics.idea: Building current requires work, stored in the magnetic field.
topics.result: $U=LI^2/2$; in a linear nondispersive medium $u_B=\mathbf B\cdot\mathbf H/2$. In vacuum $u_B=B^2/(2\mu_0)$.
topics.explain: The source must supply a voltage opposing the back emf.::Otherwise current cannot increase.;;Multiply $L\,dI/dt$ by current to get input power.::Power is voltage times current.;;Integrate $LI\,dI$ from zero to the final current.::Energy is accumulated power.;;For a solenoid insert its field and geometry to identify energy per volume.::The uniform-field limit connects circuit and field descriptions.
topics.trap: In a nonlinear or hysteretic medium, blindly using $BH/2$ can fail; incremental work depends on the path.
topics.check: If current doubles in an ideal linear inductor, how does U change?=>It quadruples.

topics.title: Charge conservation and Maxwell’s repair
topics.idea: Ampère’s original law cannot describe charge building up on a capacitor.
topics.result: $\nabla\cdot\mathbf J=-\partial\rho/\partial t$; $\nabla\times\mathbf B=\mu_0\mathbf J+\mu_0\epsilon_0\partial\mathbf E/\partial t$ in vacuum.
topics.explain:
Divergence of a curl is zero, so the old law would require $
abla\cdot J=0$ always.::Apply divergence to both sides.;;Continuity instead gives $
abla\cdot J=-\partialho/\partial t$.::Charge can accumulate locally.;;Gauss's law turns $\partialho/\partial t$ into $\epsilon_0
abla\cdot\partial E/\partial t$.::The changing charge changes electric divergence.;;Add the displacement-current term to make the total divergence zero.::This restores consistency with conservation.
topics.trap: Displacement current is not necessarily charge transport through the dielectric gap.
topics.check: What crosses an ideal vacuum capacitor gap: conduction current or displacement-current contribution?=>Displacement-current contribution.

topics.title: The four Maxwell equations
topics.idea: Four field laws connect electric and magnetic sources and changes.
topics.explain: Electric charge sources electric flux.::This is Gauss's electric law.;;Magnetic flux through a closed surface is zero.::There are no magnetic monopoles in this formulation.;;Changing magnetic field creates electric circulation.::This is Faraday's law.;;Current and changing electric field create magnetic circulation.::This is Ampère-Maxwell law.
topics.trap: The vacuum equations use total charge/current. In matter, switching to free sources also requires D and H.
topics.check: Which equation forbids a net magnetic flux from a closed surface?=>$\nabla\cdot B=0$.

topics.title: Maxwell equations in matter
topics.idea: D and H absorb the bound-charge and magnetization contributions.
topics.explain: Separate total charge into free and bound charge.::P represents the bound electric response.;;Separate current into free, magnetization and polarization currents.::Changing P is also a current contribution.;;Use $D=\epsilon_0E+P$ and $H=B/\mu_0-M$.::These definitions collect the material terms.;;Supply constitutive relations to solve a particular medium.::Four differential laws alone do not specify its response.
topics.trap: $\partial_tD$ includes both vacuum and polarization terms; it is not always just $\epsilon_0\partial_tE$.
topics.check: In a homogeneous linear dielectric, what is the displacement-current density?=>$\epsilon\,\partial E/\partial t$.

topics.title: Electromagnetic boundary conditions
topics.idea: Surface charges and currents determine the allowed field jumps.
topics.explain: Use thin pillboxes for D and B.::Only the normal cap flux survives.;;Use shrinking loops for E and H.::Only tangential circulation and any sheet current survive.;;Keep n directed from medium 1 to 2 in all four relations.::A consistent orientation fixes the signs.;;The formulas assume finite nonsingular fields at an ordinary stationary interface.::Flux derivative terms vanish with the shrinking loop area.
topics.trap: Continuity of tangential H requires zero free surface current; continuity of normal D requires zero free surface charge.
topics.check: With $K_f=0$, is tangential B always continuous?=>No. H is continuous; B can change if permeability changes.

questions.prompt: State local Ohm’s law, define conductivity and distinguish it from resistivity.
questions.answer: For an isotropic conductor at rest, $\mathbf J=\sigma\mathbf E$. Conductivity σ has units S/m; resistivity is $\varrho=1/\sigma$ in Ω m. It is an empirical linear response, not a universal law for all materials.
questions.final: $J=\sigma E$; $\varrho=1/\sigma$.

questions.prompt: Derive the resistance of a uniform wire of length ℓ and area A from local Ohm’s law.
questions.answer: Use $J=I/A$ and $E=V/\ell$. Then $I/A=\sigma V/\ell$, giving $V/I=\ell/(\sigma A)$. The assumptions are uniform conductivity, cross-section and steady current.
questions.final: $R=\ell/(\sigma A)$.

questions.prompt: Define emf and explain why its name can be misleading.
questions.answer: Emf is closed-path driving work per unit charge, $\mathcal E=\oint\mathbf f\cdot d\mathbf l$. It has units J/C = volt. It is not a mechanical force and need not equal the loaded source's terminal voltage.
questions.final: Emf measures energy per charge, in volts.

questions.prompt: Can a purely electrostatic field provide a nonzero emf around a closed loop? Explain.
questions.answer: No. $\mathbf E=-\nabla V$ for a single-valued electrostatic potential, so $\oint E\cdot dl=0$. A battery needs a non-electrostatic source force; an induced electric field is not electrostatic.
questions.final: Purely electrostatic closed-loop emf is zero.

questions.prompt: A 0.40 m rod moves at 3.0 m/s perpendicular to a 0.50 T field and to its own length. Find the emf magnitude.
questions.answer: $\mathcal E=B\ell v=(0.50)(0.40)(3.0)=0.60$ V. Charge separation is along $\mathbf v\times\mathbf B$; the positive end depends on the stated vector directions.
questions.final: $\mathcal E=0.60$ V.

questions.prompt: If magnetic forces do no work on individual charges, where does the heat in a moving-rod circuit come from?
questions.answer: The pulling agent works against magnetic drag on the current-carrying rod. In steady motion its mechanical power equals the resistor's heating power. Magnetic forces redirect motion but supply no net work on a charge.
questions.final: The external mechanical agent supplies the energy.

questions.prompt: State Lenz’s rule and distinguish opposition to flux from opposition to flux change.
questions.answer: The induced current produces magnetic effects opposing the change in linked flux. If an existing flux decreases, the induced field acts in the same direction as that flux to oppose its decrease.
questions.final: The opposition is to change, not always to the field itself.

questions.prompt: List three ways to change the flux through a flat loop in uniform B.
questions.answer: Since $\Phi_B=BA\cos\theta$, changing B, loop area A or orientation θ can change flux. θ is measured from the area normal. A nonzero flux does not by itself imply an emf.
questions.final: Emf requires a time derivative of linked flux.

questions.prompt: Can there be induced E at a location containing no conductor? Give the governing law.
questions.answer: Yes. $\nabla\times E=-\partial B/\partial t$ describes a field in space. A wire merely provides mobile charges that respond; the induced E exists without it.
questions.final: Changing magnetic flux produces electric circulation without a wire.

questions.prompt: Why cannot a general induced E be described using only a single-valued scalar electrostatic potential?
questions.answer: A gradient has zero curl and zero closed-loop integral. A changing B gives $\oint E\cdot dl=-d\Phi_B/dt$, which can be nonzero. Thus $E=-\nabla V$ alone is insufficient.
questions.final: Nonzero circulation rules out a purely scalar electrostatic description.

questions.prompt: Define self-inductance and the henry, stating the linearity assumption.
questions.answer: For a fixed linear circuit, flux linkage is $N\Phi=LI$. One henry corresponds to one weber-turn per ampere, or an induced emf magnitude of one volt when current changes at one ampere per second.
questions.final: $L=N\Phi/I$ in henries for a linear circuit.

questions.prompt: Distinguish the induced emf of an ideal inductor from its passive terminal voltage drop.
questions.answer: The induced emf opposes the current change: $\mathcal E_L=-L\,dI/dt$. With current entering the positive-labelled terminal, the passive drop is $v_L=+L\,dI/dt$. They describe the same induction with different sign conventions.
questions.final: Back emf is negative relative to increasing current; passive drop is positive.

questions.prompt: Define mutual inductance and explain why coil orientation matters.
questions.answer: Linkage in coil 2 due to $I_1$ is $\lambda_{21}=MI_1$. Then $\mathcal E_2=-M\,dI_1/dt$. Reversing one coil's reference normal changes the signed linkage and M, while its coupling magnitude is unchanged.
questions.final: State winding directions or use a consistent dot convention.

questions.prompt: Find the energy of a 0.30 H inductor carrying 2.0 A. What happens if current is reversed without changing magnitude?
questions.answer: $U=LI^2/2=(0.30)(4)/2=0.60$ J. Since energy depends on $I^2$, reversing I changes field direction but not stored energy for an ideal linear inductor.
questions.final: $U=0.60$ J for either current direction.

questions.prompt: Write and interpret the local continuity equation.
questions.answer: $\partial\rho/\partial t+\nabla\cdot J=0$. A positive net outward current from a tiny volume reduces its charge density. This is local conservation of electric charge.
questions.final: Charge accumulation balances net inward current.

questions.prompt: What is displacement current in vacuum? Does it require charge carriers crossing the surface?
questions.answer: Its density is $J_d=\epsilon_0\partial E/\partial t$, and its integrated contribution is $I_d=\epsilon_0d\Phi_E/dt$. It can occur through a vacuum capacitor gap with no conduction carriers crossing.
questions.final: Displacement current is a changing-field contribution to magnetic circulation.

questions.prompt: Show that the divergence of a magnetic field vanishes, and state its integral form.
questions.answer:
$\oint B\cdot da=0$ and $
abla\cdot B=0$. Writing $B=
abla	imes A$ gives $
abla\cdot B=
abla\cdot(
abla	imes A)=0$ because mixed derivatives cancel for a smooth vector potential. Thus magnetic field lines have no net source or sink: as much flux enters a closed surface as leaves it.
questions.final: No magnetic monopole source appears in these equations.
tags: Prerequisite-course PYQ A26 Q15 · adapted marks

questions.prompt: Write Faraday’s law in differential form and explain each side.
questions.answer: $\nabla\times E=-\partial B/\partial t$. The left side measures local electric circulation per area; the right side gives the opposing rate of magnetic-field change.
questions.final: Changing B generates circulating E.

questions.prompt: State Ampère-Maxwell law in matter and identify the sources on its right side.
questions.answer: $\nabla\times H=J_f+\partial D/\partial t$. The first term is free conduction/current density; the second includes vacuum and polarization response because $D=\epsilon_0E+P$.
questions.final: The H curl is driven by free current plus changing D.

questions.prompt: Why is normal B continuous at an ordinary interface, even if permeability changes?
questions.answer: A thin pillbox and $\oint B\cdot da=0$ give $B_{2n}=B_{1n}$. Permeability affects the corresponding H components, but there is no magnetic surface charge in Maxwell's equations.
questions.final: Normal B is continuous.

questions.prompt: A wire has ℓ=2 m, A=$1.0\times10^{-6}$ m² and σ=$5.0\times10^7$ S/m. Apply 0.10 V. Find R, I, E, J and total power.
questions.answer: $R=\ell/(\sigma A)=0.040$ Ω.::The wire is uniform and ohmic.;;$I=V/R=2.5$ A and $E=V/\ell=0.050$ V/m.::Use the terminal voltage along its length.;;$J=\sigma E=2.5\times10^6$ A/m², also $I/A$.::Local and global current descriptions must agree.;;$P=VI=0.25$ W; equivalently $JE(A\ell)=0.25$ W.::Field power density integrates to the circuit power.

questions.prompt: A 12 V source of internal resistance 1 Ω drives a 5 Ω load. Find current, terminal voltage and the power budget.
questions.answer: The closed-loop equation is $12=I(1+5)$.::Both resistances carry the same current.;;I=2 A and $V_{\rm term}=12-Ir=10$ V.::Internal voltage drop reduces the external voltage.;;Source power is $\mathcal EI=24$ W; internal heating is $I^2r=4$ W and load power is $I^2R=20$ W.::Energy supplied equals total dissipation.
questions.final: I=2 A, terminal voltage 10 V; 24 W supplied = 4 W internal + 20 W load.

questions.prompt: The rod in Q5 completes a circuit of total resistance 2 Ω. Find current, magnetic drag and pulling power at constant speed.
questions.answer: $I=\mathcal E/R=0.60/2=0.30$ A.::The circuit is resistive and induction transients are neglected.;;$F=B I\ell=(0.50)(0.30)(0.40)=0.060$ N opposite motion.::Lenz's law fixes the drag direction.;;$P_{\rm pull}=Fv=0.18$ W and $I^2R=0.18$ W.::Steady motion leaves no kinetic-energy increase.
questions.final: I=0.30 A, drag=0.060 N, input power=0.18 W equals heating.

questions.prompt: A 200-turn coil of area 0.010 m² has its normal along a field that rises uniformly from 0.10 T to 0.40 T in 0.050 s. Find its emf, including sign.
questions.answer: Choose positive normal along B, so $\Phi_B=BA$.::The angle is zero.;;$dB/dt=0.30/0.050=6.0$ T/s.::The ramp is uniform.;;$\mathcal E=-NA\,dB/dt=-200(0.010)(6.0)=-12$ V.::Use total linkage rather than one-turn flux.
questions.final: −12 V in the positive-loop orientation; magnitude 12 V.

questions.prompt: A coil has N turns and area A and rotates with angular speed ω in uniform B. Derive its sinusoidal emf when its normal initially points along B.
questions.answer: The angle is $\theta=\omega t$, giving linkage $\lambda=NAB\cos\omega t$.::Rotation changes orientation, not B or A.;;Differentiate: $d\lambda/dt=-NAB\omega\sin\omega t$.::The chain rule contributes ω.;;Faraday's minus sign gives $\mathcal E=NAB\omega\sin\omega t$.::The emf opposes the signed flux change.;;At maximum linkage the emf is zero; at zero linkage its magnitude is maximum.::A slope is not the same as the function value.
questions.final: Peak emf $\mathcal E_0=NAB\omega$.

questions.prompt: Uniform $B(t)\hat z$ occupies a circular region of radius a. Derive the azimuthal E for r<a, with positive circulation counterclockwise viewed from +z.
questions.answer: Choose a concentric circle of radius r.::Axial symmetry makes E tangential and constant.;;The enclosed flux is $B\pi r^2$.::The whole surface lies within the field region.;;$E_\phi(2\pi r)=-\pi r^2\dot B$.::Apply Faraday's law with the right-hand normal +z.;;Thus $E_\phi=-(r/2)\dot B$.::Divide by circumference.
questions.final: Inside: $\mathbf E=-(r/2)\dot B\,\hat{\boldsymbol\phi}$.

questions.prompt: For Q26 find E at r>a and evaluate its magnitude for a=0.10 m, r=0.20 m and $\dot B=4$ T/s.
questions.answer: Only the disk contributes flux, so $\Phi=B\pi a^2$.::B is zero outside the disk.;;$2\pi r E_\phi=-\pi a^2\dot B$, hence $E_\phi=-a^2\dot B/(2r)$.::The path circumference still uses r.;;The magnitude is $(0.10)^2(4)/(2\times0.20)=0.10$ V/m.::Substitute in SI units.;;The inside and outside formulas agree at r=a.::This checks continuity at the boundary.
questions.final: Outside: $E_\phi=-a^2\dot B/(2r)$; magnitude 0.10 V/m here.

questions.prompt: Derive L for a long solenoid with N turns, length ℓ, area A and uniform linear permeability μ.
questions.answer: Inside, $H=NI/\ell$ and $B=\mu NI/\ell$.::Neglect end effects and use the free-current circulation law.;;Each turn links $\Phi=BA$.::The field is approximately uniform over the cross-section.;;Total linkage is $N\Phi=\mu N^2AI/\ell$.::N identical turns link the same flux.;;Divide linkage by current.::Inductance is defined by $\lambda=LI$.
questions.final: $L=\mu N^2A/\ell$.

questions.prompt: Two ideal coaxial long coils share area $2\times10^{-4}$ m² and length 0.20 m, with 500 and 1000 turns. In air, find M and the emf magnitude in coil 2 when $dI_1/dt=3$ A/s.
questions.answer: Coil 1 makes $B_1=\mu_0N_1I_1/\ell$.::Assume all of its uniform interior flux links coil 2.;;$\lambda_{21}=N_2B_1A=MI_1$, so $M=\mu_0N_1N_2A/\ell$.::Use the common cross-sectional area.;;$M=6.283\times10^{-4}$ H.::Substitute the specified geometry.;;$\lvert\mathcal E_2\rvert=M\lvert\dot I_1\rvert=1.885\times10^{-3}$ V.::Faraday's law differentiates linkage.
questions.final: M=0.6283 mH; induced emf magnitude 1.885 mV.

questions.prompt: Derive the stored energy of a constant-L inductor from the work supplied by a source.
questions.answer: The source balances passive inductor drop $v=L\,dI/dt$.::It must overcome the opposing induced emf.;;Power is $p=vI=LI\,dI/dt$.::Power delivered equals voltage times current.;;Energy increment is $dU=p\,dt=LI\,dI$.::Time cancels in the differential expression.;;Integrate from zero to I: $U=L\int_0^I I'\,dI'=LI^2/2$.::L is constant and initial field energy is zero.
questions.final: $U=LI^2/2$ for a linear inductor.

questions.prompt: Find the vacuum magnetic energy density for B=0.020 T, and the energy in 0.010 m³ of uniform field.
questions.answer: $u_B=B^2/(2\mu_0)$.::The region is vacuum, so $H=B/\mu_0$.;;$u_B=0.0004/(8\pi\times10^{-7})=159.2$ J/m³.::Square B before dividing.;;$U=u_BV=1.592$ J.::The energy density is uniform.

questions.prompt: An ideal parallel-plate vacuum capacitor has area A and charging current I. Show that the displacement current through the gap equals I.
questions.answer: $E=Q/(\epsilon_0A)$ between the plates away from edges.::Gauss's law gives the uniform field.;;Electric flux through the plate area is $\Phi_E=EA=Q/\epsilon_0$.::Use the same area that the conduction-current loop spans.;;$I_d=\epsilon_0d\Phi_E/dt=dQ/dt=I$.::The change in charge creates the change in flux.;;Thus a surface cutting the wire and a surface bulging through the gap give the same total Ampère-Maxwell contribution.::The extra term removes surface-choice inconsistency.
questions.final: $I_d=I$ for the complete plate area.

questions.prompt: Write the four integral Maxwell equations for a fixed loop/surface in vacuum, explaining the source or change in each.
questions.answer: $\oint_S E\cdot da=Q_{\rm enc}/\epsilon_0$.::Enclosed electric charge produces electric flux.;;$\oint_S B\cdot da=0$.::No magnetic charge sources net closed-surface flux.;;$\oint_C E\cdot dl=-d\int_S B\cdot da/dt$.::Changing magnetic flux produces electric circulation.;;$\oint_C B\cdot dl=\mu_0I_{\rm enc}+\mu_0\epsilon_0d\int_S E\cdot da/dt$.::Both conduction and changing electric flux produce magnetic circulation.;;In magnetostatics the displacement term vanishes, leaving $\oint B\cdot dl=\mu_0I_{\rm enc}$, the original integral Ampère law.::All fields are time-independent.;;For curl laws, C is the boundary of S and their orientations obey the right-hand rule.::A consistent sign requires paired path and surface directions.
questions.final: The two flux laws and two circulation laws form Maxwell's system.
tags: Legacy PYQ N25 Q6 · expanded to Maxwell system

questions.prompt: Show how changing polarization contributes to current and enters Ampère-Maxwell law in matter.
questions.answer: A changing dipole density means charges shift locally, giving $J_p=\partial P/\partial t$.::Current includes bound charge motion.;;Total current is $J=J_f+\nabla\times M+\partial P/\partial t$.::Magnetization loops and polarization changes are both bound contributions.;;Insert this into vacuum-form Ampère-Maxwell and move curl M left.::Separate the material current terms.;;The result is $\nabla\times H=J_f+\partial(\epsilon_0E+P)/\partial t$.::Use the definition of H.
questions.final: $\nabla\times H=J_f+\partial D/\partial t$.

questions.target: Boundary jump from a sheet current
questions.prompt: An interface has normal $\hat n=\hat z$ from medium 1 to 2 and free surface current $K_f=K\hat x$. What tangential H jump is required? Also state the normal B condition.
questions.answer: Write $\Delta H=H_2-H_1$. The condition is $\hat z\times\Delta H=K\hat x$.::A narrow Amperian loop encloses the sheet current.;;Since $\hat z\times\hat y=-\hat x$, $\Delta H_t=-K\hat y$.::Choose the component with the required cross product.;;Normal B satisfies $B_{2z}=B_{1z}$.::A magnetic pillbox encloses no magnetic charge.;;The normal H components require permeability information if the media differ.::B and H are not interchangeable.
questions.final: $H_{2t}-H_{1t}=-K\hat y$; normal B is continuous.

questions.prompt: At a stationary interface with no free surface charge/current, medium 2 has $\epsilon_2=2\epsilon_1$, $\mu_2=3\mu_1$. Relate all normal and tangential E and H components.
questions.answer: $D_{2n}=D_{1n}$ gives $E_{2n}=E_{1n}/2$.::No free surface charge is enclosed by a thin pillbox.;;$E_{2t}=E_{1t}$.::Faraday flux through a vanishing loop tends to zero for finite fields.;;$B_{2n}=B_{1n}$ gives $H_{2n}=H_{1n}/3$.::Normal magnetic flux is continuous.;;$H_{2t}=H_{1t}$.::There is no free sheet current.
questions.final: Normal E and H scale inversely with ε and μ; tangential E and H are continuous here.

questions.prompt: Define line, surface and volume current measures, derive charge continuity, then explain Maxwell’s correction to Ampère’s law using a charging capacitor.
questions.answer:
For line charge density λ moving along a wire at speed v, $I=\lambda v$ in A. Surface current density is $K=\sigma_qv$ in A/m, and volume current density is $J=ho v$ in A/m² for a single moving charge population.::Each is charge density times velocity, with the appropriate cross-section dimension.;;Charge leaving a fixed volume per time is $\oint J\cdot da=-d\intho\,d	au/dt$.::Outward flow reduces the charge remaining inside.;;The divergence theorem converts this to $\int(
abla\cdot J+\partial_tho)d	au=0$. Since every volume satisfies it, $
abla\cdot J=-\partial_tho$.::A continuous integrand whose integral vanishes in every volume must vanish locally.;;The old law is $
abla	imes B=\mu_0J$. Taking its divergence forces $
abla\cdot J=0$.::Divergence of curl vanishes identically.;;Continuity demands $
abla\cdot J=-\partial_tho$, which is nonzero where charge accumulates.::Local charge conservation must hold.;;Gauss's law gives $ho=\epsilon_0
abla\cdot E$, so $\partial_tho=\epsilon_0
abla\cdot\partial_tE$.::Differentiate the electric source law.;;Adding $\epsilon_0\partial_tE$ to J makes the total divergence zero.::The two divergence terms cancel.;;The corrected law is $
abla	imes B=\mu_0(J+\epsilon_0\partial_tE)$.::It contains conduction and displacement-current density.;;For a vacuum capacitor $E=Q/(\epsilon_0A)$, giving $I_d=\epsilon_0A\dot E=\dot Q=I$.::Both possible spanning surfaces now give identical magnetic circulation.
questions.final: Maxwell's displacement current restores charge conservation and surface independence.

questions.prompt: Compare induction in a stationary loop with induction in a moving conductor, including the correct emf expression, sign and energy source.
questions.answer: For a stationary loop, $\mathcal E=\oint E\cdot dl=-d\Phi_B/dt$.::Only the electric force contributes along a fixed path.;;For a moving material loop, $\mathcal E=\oint(E+u\times B)\cdot dl$, where u is the conductor velocity.::Charges share the conductor's transport motion.;;For an ordinary moving closed circuit, the combined expression equals the negative rate of linked flux.::Both field variation and changing surface geometry enter the flux derivative.;;The loop orientation and area normal must be paired.::Faraday's sign is meaningful only with this convention.;;Lenz's rule opposes the flux change. In a moving rod this creates drag, and the pulling work becomes electrical heating.::Energy conservation rules out self-amplifying motion.;;In a stationary coil near a changing source field, the field-generating apparatus supplies the transferred energy.::A nonconservative E can transfer energy without mechanical motion of the receiving loop.
questions.final: Stationary induction uses circulating E; motional induction includes $u\times B$; both obey the oriented flux rule under the stated conditions.

questions.prompt: Derive magnetic energy from circuit work and recover the energy density inside a long linear solenoid. Discuss assumptions.
questions.answer: The incremental source work is $dU=LI\,dI$ for constant L.::The passive voltage is $L\dot I$.;;Integration gives $U=LI^2/2$.::Start from zero current.;;A long solenoid has $L=\mu N^2A/\ell$ and $H=NI/\ell$.::Use its uniform interior field, neglecting ends.;;Substitute to get $U=(\mu H^2/2)A\ell$.::Replace current and turns by H.;;Divide by field volume $A\ell$ to get $u_B=\mu H^2/2=B\cdot H/2=B^2/(2\mu)$.::The medium is linear and isotropic.;;In vacuum use $\mu_0$. For nonlinear or hysteretic media, energy changes require the appropriate integral of $H\cdot dB$ and can include loss.::A constant proportionality no longer describes the material path.
questions.final: In a linear lossless medium, $u_B=B\cdot H/2$; in vacuum, $u_B=B^2/(2\mu_0)$.

questions.prompt: Derive the four macroscopic electromagnetic boundary conditions at a stationary ordinary interface carrying free surface charge σf and free surface current Kf.
questions.answer: Take n from medium 1 to 2 and shrink a pillbox across the surface.::This fixes the cap orientations and jump signs.;;Gauss's law for D leaves $(D_2-D_1)\cdot n=\sigma_f$.::Side flux vanishes, but enclosed sheet charge stays proportional to cap area.;;Magnetic Gauss law gives $(B_2-B_1)\cdot n=0$.::There is no magnetic surface charge.;;A tiny rectangular loop in Faraday's law gives $n\times(E_2-E_1)=0$.::The magnetic-flux derivative tends to zero with loop area for bounded fields.;;The H circulation law gives $n\times(H_2-H_1)=K_f$.::The free sheet current survives while the displacement flux through the narrow loop vanishes.;;Then use material laws, such as $D_i=\epsilon_iE_i$ and $B_i=\mu_iH_i$, to obtain jumps of other components.::Constitutive relations differ across the interface.
questions.final: Normal D jumps by σf, normal B is continuous, tangential E is continuous, and tangential H jumps according to Kf.
